big_idea: 100¢ = $1 = 1 LOONIE. Make $1 with many coin combinations.
learning_intention: We are learning to make $1 in 3 different ways.
student_learning_goal: I can make $1 in 3 different ways.
success_criteria: I can MAKE $1 with mixed coins.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Tappy + Loonie Lou — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Loonie Lou: Friends — meet the LOONIE! $1 = 100¢ = MANY coin combos! Lou opens: 'One hundred cents, ONE LOONIE LOU!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Loonie Lou the Mouse puppet (small mouse with loonie pendant). 'Money friends — yesterday we made 50¢ many ways. Today: $1 = 100¢ = MANY ways!'

Review LOONIE. 'A LOONIE is the $1 coin. GOLD. Loon bird. = 100 cents!'

Demo 3 ways for $1:
- WAY 1: 4 QUARTERS (25+25+25+25 = 100¢).
- WAY 2: 10 DIMES (10×10 = 100¢).
- WAY 3: 2 QUARTERS + 5 DIMES (50 + 50 = 100¢).

Class checks each total. 'Same value, different combo!'

'Lou says — many ways add to 100¢ = $1!'

Demo $1 = 1 LOONIE alone. 'One coin = $1 too!'

Now show $1 = 50¢ + 50¢ (using two 50¢ coins). 'Same total!'

'Lou says — when paying $1, you can use ANY combination!'

Now each pair gets Coin Cards + Record Strip. Target: $1. Find 3 ways.

'Lou says — count to 100¢ each time!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Coin Cards + Record Strip. Pairs find 3 ways to make $1.
Stretch: $1 with 8 coins or fewer (no loonie or 50¢).
STRATEGY COMPARE: 2-3 pairs share their $1 combo. Class: 'Whose used FEWEST coins? Whose used MOST? Are all $1?' Cite CGI part-whole composition.
steps.teacher_prompt: Lou: 'Same DOLLAR, different COMBOS. The MATH cares about the TOTAL.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk to coin stations. NO-MATERIALS PATH: children use 10 fingers as 10¢ each (10 fingers = $1 = 10 dimes), OR tap the carpet 4 times for 4 quarters.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: makes $1; verifies; records; finds 3; explains.

consolidation.exit_routine: Lou's Loonie Cheer — class chants: 'One hundred cents, ONE LOONIE LOU! Many coin combos make a buck for YOU!' (3x). Then the unit refrain 'SAME AMOUNT — MANY WAYS! TAP TO PAY!' Each child writes one $1 combo on a sticky.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child uses 4 quarters + 1 quarter = $1 — repairing the over-shoot trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On '$1 = 100¢ many ways', the trap is target-monitoring failure: child counts on without anchoring to the target (Carpenter & Moser CGI 'join-result-unknown' chains; Sowder 1992 on quantitative units). Without target-anchoring, children build 85¢ or 110¢ instead of 100¢.

Yesterday Tappy showed three ways to 50¢. Today Lou builds the loonie: 100¢ = TWO 50¢ stacks (forward-link from L1) OR 4 quarters OR 10 dimes OR mixed combos. Lesson 3 bills + coins; Lesson 4 hundreds; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Lou asks — count by 25s. 25, 50, 75, 100, 125. 5 quarters = ___?'

Probe. '5 quarters = 125¢ = $1.25. We need EXACTLY $1 = 100¢. So 4 quarters!'

Generalise. 'Lou says — STOP at the target. 4 quarters = $1, exactly.'

If still over: count up out loud. '25, 50, 75, 100 — STOP!'
common_misconceptions: Round numbers ok. (Repair: must equal target.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child counts past 100¢: drill target-monitoring — child says 'I'm at ___, I need ___ more to reach 100' BEFORE adding the next coin.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child stops short of 100¢: fingers-as-coins drill (10 fingers = 10 dimes = $1); child re-builds with fingers first.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can build $1 one way but not another: hide the canonical 4-quarter solution; force a non-quarter route.

parts_outline.task: For 3 combos, mark TRUE if total = $1.
Make $1 using ONLY nickels — how many?
